messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH 5xx rate detected for gateway-proxy in region eu-west1. Alert details: 5xx-rate=9.4% over 5m, p50 latency ↑ 350ms, inflight queue growth. Runbook -> https://runbooks.internal/incidents/gateway-5xx (pager class: page)

maya (oncall): taking this. I’m oncall for eu-west1. starting triage.

samir (eng-sre): on my way. can you paste the top error? I’m already looking at proxy logs and backend mlworker metrics.

maya (oncall): top error is a repeated backend 502 from model-worker pool. snippets:
```
[proxy] upstream_response_time=0.42, status=502, backend=mlworker-alloc-12
[mlworker] ERROR: model inference worker OOM, killed pid=2345, trace=kv-cache-miss
```

leo (netops): seeing increased retry rates to egress cluster eu-west1-egress-01. Connections to eu-north are healthy. nets: no route flaps, but connpool exhausted on egress-proxy nodes: conn_count ~ 6500 vs soft-limit 6000.

samir (eng-sre): looks like a cascade: mlworker pods thrashing -> backend 502 -> proxy retries -> connpool pressure -> 5xx amplification. Suggest isolating mlworker pool and activating circuit-breaker in front of it to prevent retries.

maya (oncall): starting mitigation: 1) apply circuit-breaker to mlworker-target group; 2) scale gateway-proxy replicas; 3) shift a fraction of traffic to eu-north as failover. Executing step 1 now.

ops-runner-bot: exec: runbook.apply --team=eng-sre --play=circuit-breaker-mlworker --region=eu-west1

ops-runner-bot: output: OK -> circuit-breaker set: max_retries=0, health_threshold=20s for target group mlworker-euw1

samir (eng-sre): for transparency, command I ran to inspect pods:
```
kubectl -n gateway get pods -l app=gateway-proxy -o wide
kubectl -n model get pods -l role=mlworker -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, status:.status.phase, restartCount:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}'
```

maya (oncall): scaling gateway-proxy to 24 replicas to absorb burst.

ops-runner-bot: kubectl scale deploy/gateway-proxy --replicas=24 -n gateway -> accepted

leo (netops): ready to flip routing. If we shift too much traffic there may be cold-cache penalties. Recommend start with 20% to eu-north, monitor error rate for 2m.

maya (oncall): initiating smart-router shift: prefer eu-north weight +20% for route /v1/generate. command:
```
routerctl set-weight --route /v1/generate --from eu-west1 --to eu-north --weight 0.2
```

ops-runner-bot: routerctl output: success. new weights applied.

jin (product-safety): heads-up: customers with pinned model versions may hit model mismatch if routed cross-region. tagging customer-impact thresholds and alerting CS.

cs-team-bot: auto-detect: tenants exceeding error-threshold -> tenant-a, tenant-b. Creating high-priority tickets and starting outreach; templated note queued.

samir (eng-sre): monitoring metrics:
- pre-mitigation 5xx: 9.4%
- after circuit-breaker + scale + 20% shift: 5xx -> 2.1% after 90s
- p50 latency dropped back to 120ms in eu-north; eu-west1 p50 around 280ms

maya (oncall): good improvement. I'm keeping circuit-breaker enforced for 15m window and keeping the router shift for 10m, then will evaluate rollback to normal weights.

leo (netops): noticed one side-effect: KV cache hit rate in eu-west1 dropped ~30% after shifting 20% traffic. Could see temporary extra upstream load when we shift back. Documenting for handover.

samir (eng-sre): we should also drain problematic mlworker pods to stop OOM loop. I'll cordon+drain the top offenders.

samir (eng-sre): commands run:
```
kubectl cordon mlworker-alloc-12
kubectl drain mlworker-alloc-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

ops-runner-bot: drain complete for mlworker-alloc-12. New pods scheduled gradually. No immediate crashloops observed.

maya (oncall): performing handoff: I need to go offline in 12m. samir, please take lead for active monitoring and rollback plan. key points in handoff:
- circuit-breaker active
- router shift +20% to eu-north
- gateway-proxy scaled to 24
- drained the offending mlworker pods
- customers impacted: tenant-a and tenant-b contacted via CS
- watch for cache warmup when shifting back

samir (eng-sre): ack takeover. I'll keep watching metrics and will escalate to SRE lead if 5xx > 3% for another 6m. Also will check autoscaler behavior for gateway-proxy to ensure we don't overshoot.

jin (product-safety): please keep a short incident note: initial cause suspected: mlworker OOM cascade -> proxy retries -> connpool exhaustion. Potential follow-ups: increase mlworker memory, adjust model batching, add graceful backpressure in mlworker.

maya (oncall): filing initial incident summary and will ping on-call slack channel when I leave.

incident-bot: Incident status: MITIGATED (partial failover applied). Notes: active routing shift to eu-north, circuit-breaker enforced, problematic pods drained. Keep monitoring. Incident owner: samir (eng-sre). Incident timeline summarized in ticket INC-2026-0148.

samir (eng-sre): I'll monitor for stabilization and post a follow-up RCA draft after we confirm root cause. For now, leaving the circuit-breaker in place until OOM root fix rolled out.

cs-team-bot: Customer outreach: tenant-a & tenant-b notified at 2026-03-15T14:08Z; priority follow-up scheduled.

maya (oncall): handing off now. thanks all.

samir (eng-sre): taking over. I'll update here with any changes.
